fields.description:
Mirror inventory finding F13 (`reports/stability/mirror-inventory.md`), HIGH.

## Problem

`_validate_gate_step_ids` already exists (`llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:78`) and has
exactly ONE call site: `gate_dispatch.py:154`, `gate_name="plan-review"`. Its docstring records
why it was written — a step-id rename in the gate YAML "would otherwise make the recovery lookups
silently return `None` and degrade a recoverable run to INDETERMINATE."

The other two gates load a doc at `gate_dispatch.py:437` (`code-review`) and `:697`
(`completion-verification`) and validate nothing, while each has python that looks its step ids
up BY NAME:

- **code-review** → `llm/code_review/finalize.py` declares `_STEP_VERIFY = "verify"`,
  `_STEP_DECIDE = "decide"` (`:28-29`, used at `:205,211,217,300`) and
  `STEP_ASSEMBLE_DIFF = "assemble_diff"` (`:33`). That file's own comment (`:25-27`) states the
  coupling: these "MUST track gate_dispatch.STEP_VERIFY / STEP_DECIDE ... a rename of those there
  must be mirrored here."
- **completion-verification** → `llm/workflow/completion_metrics.py:34` keys
  `_WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS` on `precheck` / `verify` / `reconcile` / `passthrough`. A rename here
  degrades even more quietly than plan-review's: the row falls through
  `_WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS.get(...)` into `_UNCLASSIFIED_FIELD`, so the timing silently lands in
  "unclassified" and NOTHING errors.

## Approach — add-parity-check at each remaining dispatch site

NOT "one line each". The validator's signature is
`_validate_gate_step_ids(doc, required, *, gate_name)`, and the only required-set that exists is
`_PLAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED_STEP_IDS`. Each remaining gate needs its own set plus a call.

**The required set must be DERIVED from the constants the dispatcher already references — not
re-typed as string literals.** Re-listing the ids would add a THIRD copy of the same fact, which
is precisely the defect class this epic exists to remove. Concretely: build code-review's set from
`finalize`'s `_STEP_VERIFY` / `_STEP_DECIDE` / `STEP_ASSEMBLE_DIFF`, and completion-verification's
from `frozenset(completion_metrics._WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS)`.

Note `completion-verification.yaml` also defines `decide` (`:34`), which no python references —
it is correctly NOT required. The set is "ids the code looks up", not "ids the YAML defines";
requiring the latter would fail the gate on any harmless new step.

Import direction is safe: `finalize.py` is a strict leaf that must not back-import
`gate_dispatch`, so `gate_dispatch` imports FROM it, which is the direction already in use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: `gate_dispatch` validates the code-review doc immediately after `_gate_doc("code-review", ...)`,
      with a required set derived from `finalize`'s step-id constants. Verified by a test that
      renames a step id in an in-memory code-review doc and asserts `GateContractError`.
- [x] AC2: the same for completion-verification after `_gate_doc("completion-verification", ...)`,
      with its set derived from `completion_metrics._WORKFLOW_STEP_FIELDS`. Verified by the
      equivalent rename test.
- [x] AC3: neither required set re-types a step id as a new string literal. Verified by a test
      asserting each set is equal to the set built from the imported constants, so a literal copy
      would have to drift to pass.
- [x] AC4: the committed gate YAMLs satisfy their own required sets, so the gates still dispatch.
      Verified by a test loading each packaged YAML and calling the validator with no error.
- [x] AC5: `decide` is NOT required for completion-verification, proving the set tracks code
      references rather than YAML contents. Verified by asserting its absence from that set.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "gate_step_ids or gate_dispatch or gate_contract" -q` — the
  rename-detection tests (AC1, AC2), the derivation tests (AC3, AC5), and the
  committed-YAML-passes test (AC4).
- `python -m pytest tests/unit -q` — proves no existing gate-dispatch test regresses, since the
  new calls run on every dispatch.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
